questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion with the main clause beginning with 'Only when'?
options: Only when she arrived did she realise the mistake.
She realised the mistake only when she arrived.
She arrived and only then realised the mistake.
The mistake was realised by her only when she arrived.
questions.answer: Only when she arrived did she realise the mistake.

questions.question: Which cleft sentence correctly restates the following sentence with the subject focused: 'It was John who broke the vase.'?
options: Who broke the vase was John.
The vase was broken by John.
John is the one who broke the vase.
It was John that broke the vase.
questions.answer: Who broke the vase was John.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical scenario where a suggestion is made conditionally?
options: If I were you, I would take the job.
If I am you, I will take the job.
If you were me, I would advise you to leave.
If you were me, you would take the job.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would take the job.

questions.question: Which sentence best demonstrates ellipsis with a formal register, omitting redundant words while maintaining clarity?
options: He left without saying goodbye; she didn’t know he was leaving.
He left, and she didn’t know he was leaving.
He left, and she had no idea he was leaving at all.
He left, and she was left wondering what had happened.
questions.answer: He left, and she had no idea he was leaving at all.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a complex conditional structure with both past perfect and past simple, expressing regret or a past mistake?
options: If I had known the rules, I would have prepared better.
If I knew the rules, I would have prepared better.
If I know the rules, I would have prepared better.
If I had the rules, I would have prepared better.
questions.answer: If I had known the rules, I would have prepared better.
